text:
maria (AE): Heads-up team — Acme Corp wants to run a Private deployment POC. Requirements: preserve original client source IP for their audit logs, keep POC egress costs low (they dislike per-EIP charges), and a minimal outbound firewall allowlist. They also asked which is better for their multi-account setup: PrivateLink per-account or routing via a central TGW. @sanjay can you outline options?

sanjay (SE): TL;DR: both work but tradeoffs. PrivateLink (interface endpoints) is simplest per-account but you will see endpoint ENI IPs as source when traffic hits our connectors unless you terminate/proxy in your VPC. If true source-ip preservation is mandatory, typical approaches are: run an in-VPC proxy that forwards X-Forwarded-For (preserves visibility) or deploy central proxies behind TGW and ensure no SNAT occurs.

anya (Customer NetOps): Clarify: if we set up interface endpoints in each account and then a proxy in the same account, will the proxy preserve the original client IP?

sanjay (SE): Yes — if the client talks to your in-account proxy (no SNAT inside your network) and that proxy establishes the outbound connection to Redwood, the proxy can include the original IP in headers or avoid rewriting source if it's a TCP pass-through. But note: AWS interface endpoints terminate at ENIs; connection from ENI to our service may appear to come from endpoint ENI's IP. So the safest pattern to keep source-ip in our logs is to host the proxy in your VPC and have Redwood accept X-Forwarded-For in secure mode for the POC. We'll validate header authenticity during the POC.

tom (NetEng): For our runbook/sgs, ask them for: spoke VPC CIDRs, endpoint subnet IDs, whether they're using TGW, and their desired failure mode (fallback to public egress?). Small SG snippet we give: 
```
# sample SG for in-VPC outbound proxy
Inbound: TCP 443 from client_subnets (your app subnets)
Outbound: TCP 443 to Redwood connector IP ranges (we will provide region list)
# If using interface endpoint, allow outbound to the VPC endpoint ENIs in your account
```

maria (AE): Egress cost question: are we recommending EIPs, NAT GW, or PrivateLink? What's the POC cost posture?

sanjay (SE): For a short POC: PrivateLink avoids NAT/GW hourly costs but AWS charges for interface endpoints (hourly + per-GB). NAT Gateway has a ~$0.045/GB plus hourly per NAT. EIPs aren't charged by themselves but NAT/EIP combos incur NAT charges. If they want to minimize AWS costs, use per-account interface endpoints for small traffic or a TGW with customer-hosted proxies to avoid NAT. Redwood does not bill for those AWS primitives — we bill on inference usage and any Dedicated reservations.

security (GRC): We'll need the completed security questionnaire network section. We can prefill: TLS 1.2+ required, mTLS or API key auth, endpoint flow logs enabled, restrict to specific subnets, and customer-managed KMS if on private deploy. Also request that they enable VPC Flow Logs for the subnets used in the POC.

anya (Customer NetOps): Can you give us example firewall rules (FQDN or IP blocks) we can paste to our firewall team for the POC?

sanjay (SE): Example allowlist snippet for their outbound firewall: 
```
- destination host: connector.us-east-1.redwood-inference.internal (TLS 443)
- example dest IPs (sample): 18.204.10.0/24, 3.212.45.0/24  # concrete list to follow by region
- protocol: TCP 443
- note: if using PrivateLink, allow to interface endpoint ENI IPs created in your account
```
We'll send the authoritative per-region IP ranges once the POC region is confirmed.

maria (AE): Can we provide a one-page POC checklist so Acme's ops team knows the handoff steps?

sanjay (SE): Suggested checklist: 
1) Customer: decide PrivateLink per-account vs TGW-central proxy approach.
2) Customer: provision interface endpoints or TGW routes and share subnet IDs + SGs.
3) Customer: open outbound firewall to allowlist above.
4) Customer: optionally deploy in-VPC proxy if preserving src ip.
5) Redwood: provide connector IP list, verify mTLS/API key configuration, run connectivity tests.
6) Joint: run curl tests and confirm X-Forwarded-For / flow log evidence.

security (GRC): We'll fill recommended answers on the questionnaire once they attach it. Include a note: "Redwood requires flow logs and documented subnets for Private Deploy POCs."

deploy-bot: connectivity-check queued for thread 1791122334 — paste curl output here when you run tests. :robot_face:

anya (Customer NetOps): Thanks — we'll try PrivateLink + an app-side proxy first to see if headers meet audits. I'll attach the network section of our security questionnaire and a sample curl output when ready.

maria (AE): Thanks everyone. I'll follow up with a short pricing blurb (POC estimate) and a diagram link to our Private Deploy networking doc: https://docs.redwood.ai/private-deploy/networking

sanjay (SE): Following up later today with a diagram and the concrete per-region IP ranges.

maria (AE): Closing loop for now. If anyone else has clarifications, add to this thread. :thumbsup:
